title: RBC Learn to Play Project
description: The RBC Learn to Play Project provides grants to local organizations and communities in support of building the physical literacy of Canada's kids and youth. Learn more: http://ow.ly/XRtEu

asr.full_text: Only nine percent of Canadian kids get the required sixty minutes of physical activity every day. We need to provide opportunities for kids to develop the skills, the motivation, confidence, to be physically active and physical literacy enables them to do that. We need to foundationally change behavior. This is not a physiological issue this is a psychological issue. This is a behavioral issue, and we need to get society moving more because moving matters. Our opportunity here with physical literacy is to take the time in a thoughtful way and develop the skills, the confidence, and the motivation for kids to be able to value this and for them to be motivated everyday to get out there and find their own journey, find their own way. As parents and adults, it's our job to ensure children grow up, to develop the there and find their own journey, find their own way." JARED GILLESPIER, As parents and adults, it's our job to ensure children grow up, to develop the confidence and skills they need to lead happy, healthy lives. That's why we created the RBC Learn 2 Play project. Together with PARTICIPACTION, the Public Health Agency of Canada, and Sport4Life, the project is focused on teaching kids the essential movement skills they need to participate in sport. Over the past two years, we've provided 3.6 million dollars in funding to hundreds of organizations to help build and deliver quality sport and recreational programs. Work with kids Programs like RBC Learn to Play are essential to ensure that local organizations have the means and the tools to be effective in delivering programs and services that impact the quality of life of kids. RBC Learn to Play is a game changer they've taken the basic concept of transactional granting and made it into transformational granting and I think that's huge. Play and physical activity are part of a child's healthy development. The Learn to Play Project is helping kids get active and when we learn to enjoy physical activity and sports as children we tend to continue to be active throughout life. We know that physical activity increases quality of life, self-esteem, social interactions, and academic performance in kids. We're incredibly proud of this program and what it has achieved, but we know there's still more to do. It's an exciting time, and we can't wait for what's next.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents the RBC Learn to Play Project and describes grants supporting local organizations, communities, and children's movement skills. The physical-literacy visuals and children participating in activities reinforce an educational and community-program context. Its funding and impact claims are presented as program outcomes rather than a request to invest, pay, provide credentials, or join a wealth-generating scheme.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central content is educational and programmatic: it explains physical literacy, teaches movement skills, and describes sport and recreation programs for children. The supplied evidence does not show a reward-acquisition, investment, credential-request, recruitment, or paid-earning mechanism.
